summary: Attacked the Elementary number theory area — the single roadmap ClassicalArithmeticCompletion, 8 stages CA.0 to CA.7, with 13 accepted paper routes. Two findings. The Markoff equation has no owner anywhere in the atlas although four accepted extractions route its theory, including the n-variable Markoff-Hurwitz generalisation, into CA.4, whose targets never name it; that is medium. The Schur-Siegel-Smyth trace problem is unnamed the same way, on the weight of one paper, at low severity. The head I expected to pay — an elementary entry layer planning what Mathlib already has — is clean, and the reason is that the accepted AUDIT-18 has already mapped all eight stages to the libraries more finely than my own probes did, including pre-empting a false positive of mine. The dependency bookkeeping this area keeps is correct in every case I could test, which is worth recording because the sibling part-1 area fails the same test.
checked: All 8 stages of ClassicalArithmeticCompletion (CA.0 divisibility and multiplicative arithmetic, CA.1 residues and reciprocity, CA.2 sequences and generating functions, CA.3 polynomial and matrix arithmetic, CA.4 classical Diophantine equations, CA.5 number-field arithmetic handoff, CA.6 special algebraic numbers and Mahler measure, CA.7 integral Galois modules and orders), with their full descriptions, inputs and acceptance clauses.
Eligibility, measured rather than assumed: none of the papers this session has reviewed routes to this roadmap, checked at route granularity across all 207 paper result files. No entanglement.

All 13 paper routes and their reasons in full, and the stage each lands on: CA.4 receives 6 (CHEN-24, GAMBURD-MAGEE-RONAN-19, GHOSH-SARNAK-22, KOYMANS-PAGANO, MARTIN-25, BENNETT-SIKSEK-20), CA.1 4, CA.3 3, CA.2 2, CA.6 2, and CA.0, CA.5, CA.7 none. All are `source` routes.

The library boundary, stage by stage, which was the head I expected to pay here: an elementary entry layer sits on Mathlib's strongest material, so 'plans what the library already has' should be likely. It is clean, because the accepted AUDIT-18 has already audited all eight stages (CA.0 built, CA.5 process, the other six partly built) at a finer granularity than my probes. CA.0's audit maps ten targets — gcd and Bezout with the extended Euclidean algorithm, prime factorisation, congruences and residue rings, the Chinese remainder theorem for coprime moduli and again at non-coprime moduli with the compatibility hypothesis, p-adic valuations with Legendre's formula, the arithmetic functions with multiplicativity, Dirichlet convolution, Moebius inversion at divisor sums, and general divisor-sum identities — every one to named Mathlib or Tau Ceti declarations. There is nothing here for a red team to add.

A finding of my own that dissolved against that audit, recorded because it was one reading away from being filed. CA.6 says 'Construct Mahler measure, house, Pisot/Salem classes and dynamical/height comparisons ... and multiplicative identities', and Mathlib has Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, logMahlerMeasure and mahlerMeasure_mul in Mathlib/NumberTheory/MahlerMeasure.lean and Mathlib/Analysis/Polynomial/MahlerMeasure.lean — the definition and the very multiplicativity the stage asks a worker to prove. The audit already marks that target `partial` with the note 'For complex polynomials: definition as a circle average, multiplicativity, M(p) = |lc| times the product of max(1,|alpha|) and coefficient bounds. The Mahler measure of an algebraic number (of its minimal polynomial over Z) is not defined.' That is the correct distinction, already made, so there is no finding.

A false positive of mine that the same audit had already pre-empted: searching for Pisot and Salem returns 2 Mathlib files, which reads as the classes existing. They are Salem-Spencer sets in additive combinatorics, a different Salem. The audit records exactly this — 'Searched Pisot and Salem (matches are only Salem-Spencer sets): nothing in either library' — and marks the target absent. Reading the files rather than trusting the grep is what settled it.

A calibrated-looking anomaly that dissolved on origin, the third of this kind in this area pair. CA.0's audit verdict is `built` with ten of ten targets in the libraries, yet the atlas still carries it as `status: needs_source_decomposition`, so the roadmap asks a worker to decompose a layer the accepted audit says is done. Of the 66 layers verdicted built atlas-wide, only 4 carry that status — CA.0, GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.0, AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.0 and AN.1 — which looks anomalous until the comparison class is fixed: all 907 campaign-origin audited layers carry `needs_source_decomposition` whatever their verdict, and the other 62 built layers are tauceti-origin and all carry `unknown`. The status field is constant within each origin class and says nothing about audit verdicts, so this is not a finding and not specific to this area.

The dependency bookkeeping, tested as in part 1 of the Algebraic number theory area, where it produced a finding. Here it is correct in every case available. ClassicalArithmeticCompletion declares three prerequisites — ArithmeticDynamics, DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence, KTheoryLowDegrees — and all three list it in their own `consumers`, three for three; its own eight `consumers` include GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic, which reciprocally declares it as a prerequisite. The stage-level edges agree: CA.6 requires ArithmeticDynamics:DY.1 and DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0, CA.7 requires KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.1. Nothing is stated in prose and left unrecorded.

Duplication, which for a single-roadmap area means the declared neighbours. The pair at risk is CA.6 against DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.1, whose audited target is 'Liouville's inequality with the effective constant 2^{1-d} M(alpha)^{-1} (Mahler measure)'. DT.1 consumes the Mahler measure rather than owning it — its instruction is 'Prove Liouville bounds, then reproduce a complete source proof of Roth using auxiliary polynomials, index estimates and its inequality chain', with no construction of the measure — and DT.5's 'Mahler functions' are a different object from the Mahler measure. The direction is also recorded correctly, CA.6 requiring DT.0. No mathematics is planned twice.

The negative Pell equation, routed to CA.4 by PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO with the set D-minus, rational solubility through Hasse-Minkowski, Dirichlet's theorem that primes p = 1 mod 4 lie in it, and the narrow-class-group reformulations. This is not an omission: CA.4's target is 'Pell equations' with solutions 'classified through units with positivity conventions', which covers the negative equation, and Tau Ceti has the narrow class group and totally positive elements that the reformulation needs.

Whether the Markoff material travels under another name, before calling it absent. Searched both roadmap directories for Markoff, Markov triple, Hurwitz equation, Vieta involution, descent tree, and the equation shapes xyz and x1x2x3: the only matches are two false positives, `a1XYZ` inside the projective Weierstrass cubic of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves and the triangle-group presentation x1^n = x2^m = x3^l = x1x2x3 = 1 in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps. Neither is the Markoff equation.

The distinction between two results of Smyth's, which could have produced either a wrong finding or a wrongly dismissed one. CA.6's audited target 'Selected proven lower bounds (Kronecker; Smyth, Dobrowolski, Schinzel-Zassenhaus)' is about lower bounds for the Mahler measure, and the audit correctly records Kronecker as present and the other three as absent. The Schur-Siegel-Smyth trace problem is a different problem about the trace ratio of totally positive algebraic integers, and it is not that target. Library probes for traceRatio, Schur-Siegel, Smyth, Dobrowolski and Schinzel return 0 files in both libraries; Kronecker returns 14 and 45, matching the audit.

Tau Ceti's totallyPositive material, read rather than counted, before filing the second finding. The ten files are about totally positive elements of a number field in the settings of narrow class groups, ray classes and unit signatures (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/TotallyPositive.lean, NarrowClassGroup/, Global/RayClass/, Units/Signature/). No occurrence pairs totallyPositive with a trace, Schur, Siegel or Smyth. So the predicate exists and would not be rebuilt, while the trace ratio and the constant lambda_SSS are absent.

Library trees, with their sizes printed beside every result after two wrong paths gave me false cleans earlier in this session: a full Mathlib checkout of 8556 .lean files and the Tau Ceti library tree of 5268.

findings.where: ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.4 (Classical Diophantine equations), and the atlas as a whole
findings.claim: The Markoff equation has no owner. Four accepted paper extractions route the Markoff and Markoff-Hurwitz theory into CA.4 — the coefficient-three equation with its Vieta involutions and descent tree, its extension to every level set, the trace-coordinate normalisation with the twist identifying the two forms, and the n-variable Markoff-Hurwitz equation with its moves and exceptional families — and neither CA.4's text nor any of its eight audited targets names Markoff. No other roadmap in either directory does either, and neither library has anything. The n-variable Hurwitz generalisation in particular is a distinct theory rather than a worked example of the targets CA.4 does list, which are Pell, sums of squares, elementary descent, exponential equations, linear systems, numerical semigroups and Egyptian fractions.
findings.evidence: The four routes, all to CA.4 and all accepted. PAPER-MARTIN-25: 'CA.4 explicitly owns classical Diophantine equations and elementary descent. The coefficient-three Markoff equation, positive integer tree and reduction interface are a concrete additional source in this existing direction.' PAPER-GHOSH-SARNAK-22: 'PAPER-MARTIN-25 already sources the coefficient-three Markoff equation, the Vieta involutions and the descent to (1,1,1) there, and that route is accepted. This paper extends the same carrier to every level set x1^2 + x2^2 + x3^2 - x1x2x3 = k.' PAPER-CHEN-24: 'This paper supplies the same objects in the trace-coordinate normalisation x^2+y^2+z^2-xyz = 0, the twist (x,y,z) -> (3x,3y,3z) that identifies it with the coefficient-three equation over Z[1/3] and on integral points, the group Gamma generated by ...'. PAPER-GAMBURD-MAGEE-RONAN-19: 'This paper supplies the n-variable Markoff-Hurwitz equation x1^2 + ... + xn^2 = a x1...xn + k with its moves, its exceptional families, the passage from V(Z) to V(Z+), the Cassels-style estimates of Proposition 16 and the infinite descent of Coroll[ary]'. CA.4's own description reads: 'Supply Pell equations, sums of squares, elementary descent and source-scoped exponential equations. Route general genus-one/higher-genus solutions to effective Diophantine and rational-point owners, preserving primitive and local-solubility conditions. Include linear Diophantine systems, numerical semigroups/Frobenius numbers and Egyptian-fraction identities with the precise finite or asymptotic claims.' The accepted AUDIT-18 entry for CA.4 lists eight targets — Pell equations, sums of squares, elementary descent, exponential Diophantine equations, the routing of higher-genus equations, linear Diophantine systems, numerical semigroups and Frobenius numbers, Egyptian-fraction identities — and none is Markoff; that is consistent, since an audit audits the roadmap's targets, so this is a roadmap gap rather than an audit error. A case-insensitive search of research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ and research/blueprint/roadmaps/ for Markoff returns 0 files, and for Markov returns only Markov processes, semigroups and chains in OneParameterSemigroups, Exchangeability, GeometricTopology and OptimalTransport. Searches for 'Markov triple', 'Hurwitz equation', 'Vieta involution' and 'descent tree' return 0; the equation shapes xyz and x1x2x3 return two false positives only, the term a1XYZ in ModularCurves' projective Weierstrass cubic and the triangle-group presentation in BelyiMaps. In the libraries, Markoff and markoff return 0 files in both, as does vietaInvolution; the only Markov-named files are Tau Ceti's KnotTheory/Markov.lean and probability files and Mathlib's CategoryTheory/MarkovCategory, all unrelated.
findings.fix: Name the Markoff surface as a target of CA.4, or as its own stage if the four sources are judged to carry enough weight. The target should cover the equation x^2+y^2+z^2 = 3xyz with its Vieta involutions, the descent to (1,1,1) and the uniqueness of the reduced triple, the tree structure on positive solutions, the general level sets x1^2+x2^2+x3^2-x1x2x3 = k, and the n-variable Markoff-Hurwitz equation x1^2+...+xn^2 = a x1...xn + k with its moves and exceptional families; the trace-coordinate normalisation and the twist to the coefficient-three form should be recorded as the identification between the two presentations rather than as separate carriers, which is how PAPER-CHEN-24 routes it. Since PAPER-MARTIN-25 is already the accepted owner of the coefficient-three carrier, the cheapest correct fix is to add the target and note that carrier as its source, then let the other three routes extend it.

findings.where: ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.6 (Special algebraic numbers and Mahler measure)
findings.claim: The Schur-Siegel-Smyth trace problem is not named by CA.6 or by anything else in the atlas, although PAPER-SMITH-24 routes its classical material there. CA.6's targets cover the Mahler measure, the house, the Pisot and Salem classes, selected Mahler-measure lower bounds, finiteness statements and roots of unity; none of them is about the trace of a totally positive algebraic integer. Severity is low rather than medium because only one paper routes it and the material does sit inside CA.6's stated subject of special algebraic numbers, so the gap is that no target names it rather than that it is unplanned in principle.
findings.evidence: PAPER-SMITH-24's route to CA.6 reads: 'CA.6 plans special algebraic numbers and the Mahler measure — the house, the Pisot and Salem classes, selected lower bounds and finiteness statements through exact conjugate data — which is MSC 11R06, the same classification as the trace problem. The classical material routed there is the notion of a totally positive algebraic integer with its trace ratio, the constant lambda_SSS with the chain of bounds from Schur's e^{1/2} <= lambda_SS[S]'. The route itself argues the placement from the MSC class, which is the tell that no target names it. CA.6's description names 'Mahler measure, house, Pisot/Salem classes and dynamical/height comparisons' and 'selected lower bounds, finiteness statements and multiplicative identities', with no mention of a trace. The accepted AUDIT-18 entry for CA.6 has seven targets and none concerns the trace; its nearest one, 'Selected proven lower bounds (Kronecker; Smyth, Dobrowolski, Schinzel-Zassenhaus)', is about lower bounds for the Mahler measure — a different result of Smyth's from the trace problem, a distinction worth stating because the shared name invites confusion. Searches of both roadmap directories for 'trace problem' and 'totally positive algebraic integer' return 0 files. In the libraries, traceRatio, Schur-Siegel, Smyth, Dobrowolski and Schinzel each return 0 files in both, while Kronecker returns 14 and 45, matching the audit's note that Kronecker's theorem is present. Tau Ceti's ten totallyPositive files were read: they concern totally positive elements in narrow class group, ray class and unit signature settings, and no occurrence pairs totallyPositive with a trace, so the predicate exists but the trace ratio does not.
findings.fix: Add a target to CA.6 for the trace problem: the trace ratio tr(alpha)/deg(alpha) of a totally positive algebraic integer, the constant lambda_SSS as the infimum of that ratio over the non-rational cases, and the proven chain of lower bounds beginning with Schur's, with Lehmer-style and full Schur-Siegel-Smyth resolution explicitly kept out of scope as CA.6 already does for the Lehmer conjecture. Tau Ceti's IsTotallyPositive should be named as the predicate to consume so that the trace ratio is defined on the existing carrier rather than a new one.
